 | [0088](adr/0088-reference-interpreter-as-oracle.md) | **Reference interpreter as the executable spec & conformance oracle (not a runtime target)** — "rian-vm" was three proposals in one name (interpreter / runtime VM / playground engine); separating them *is* the decision. **Build P1:** `Rian.Eval`, a small **total tree-walking** evaluator over `Rian.Core` — a pure Core consumer like an emitter (no fork, no bytecode, no GC, sequential-only), **promoted to the conformance oracle** via an `:eval` lane in `Rian.ConformanceTest` (`eval == each emitter`). This **inverts the hierarchy**: a BEAM/`eval` disagreement is a BEAM bug, not the spec. **P3:** the playground engine = P1 → WASM/JS, shipping **ahead** of self-host → JS (amends ADR-0052). **Reject P2** (bytecode VM as a runtime target) on the charter — ADR-0000 no-separate-runtime + ADR-0050 no-fork + ADR-0057 native concurrency (removes the VM's purpose) + ADR-0058 (widens the honesty matrix) + ADR-0063 (competes with self-host); **defer-not-forbid** (Elena's dissent: a future VM's precondition *is* the oracle, so P1-first is path-independent). Reject P4 (status quo, too slow) / P5 (bytecode interchange, out of scope). Anti-drift gate: `:eval` may only run constructs ≥1 emitter supports. Naming: the debate's `Rian.Interp` is **already** the interpolation desugar (ADR-0069) → `Rian.Eval` | Proposed |
 | [0089](adr/0089-portable-bytes-and-bitreader.md) | **Portable `Bytes` type + `BitReader`/`BitWriter` API — the portable surface for byte data** — answers ADR-0078's "what is the *portable* byte surface?" Erlang's `<<seg::spec>>` (ADR-0078) is the **gold standard** for binary parsing and the transpiler round-trip, but it is a BEAM idiom (sub-byte, endianness-in-spec, destructuring); only its **byte-aligned subset** is portable. Rather than a competing bit *syntax*, adopt a `Bytes` *type* (→ BEAM `binary`, Rust `Vec<u8>`/`&[u8]`, JS `Uint8Array`, JVM `ByteArray`) + a zero-alloc `(Bytes, offset)` **`BitReader`/`BitWriter`** prelude API (ADR-0047) — the type+API pattern every target uses natively (Rust `bytes`/JS `DataView`/JVM `ByteBuffer`; Gleam restricts `<<>>` to a portable subset, Crystal/Zig use a `Bytes` library). Big-endian default + explicit `_le`; reads return `Result` (no silent truncation, ADR-0035). The byte-aligned `<<…>>` subset **lowers through** this API (one runtime, one reach story); **sub-byte stays BEAM-only by design**. No new literal syntax (`b"…"` deferred, ADR-0065); no external dep (no `bitvec`, ADR-0049 §3); portable across all Tier-1 **together** (ADR-0049 §5a / ADR-0085 anti-sprawl), reach claimed only when the ADR-0087 harness is green, sequenced behind self-host parity (ADR-0063) | Accepted (direction) |
 | [0090](adr/0090-purescript-js-as-playground-engine.md) | **PureScript → JS is the playground engine; purerl is the parity oracle** — the constraint ADR-0052/0088 designed around (an *Elixir* compiler with no browser path) is removed by ADR-0084: **PureScript's native backend is JavaScript** (stock `purs`, no WASM), so the same sources being ported compile to **browser + node JS for free**. Decision: the live "edit, see it run" engine is the **whole real compiler** (`Lexer→…→Reach→Rian.JS`) compiled by `purs`→JS and run client-side (emitted user JS in a sandboxed iframe/Worker). **Re-frames ADR-0084:** the port's *primary* deliverable is the JS compiler (browser playground + npm/node CLI); **purerl/BEAM is recast as the parity oracle** (byte-equality vs the Elixir reference) + the self-host/BEAM-retention path — type-safety-over-Dialyzer stands as a *means*, not the motive. **Supersedes ADR-0088 §3** (interpreter→WASM as the *engine*; `Rian.Eval` keeps its §1–2/§6 **oracle** role) and **demotes ADR-0052's self-host→JS gate** to a later language milestone (a free Rian-on-JS ≡ PureScript-on-JS cross-check). Ride the next emitter step (`Rian.JS`, port-plan Part A — its `annotate`/`ic` prereq has landed) + a JS build profile (standard package set; stub the one `HostRef` FFI; skip `Beam` in-browser). Anti-drift: one source, two backends, **one parity corpus** (§6). BEAM-in-WASM / server-side compile stay rejected | Proposed |
+| [0091](adr/0091-by-example-corpus-as-gated-tour-source.md) | **The by-example corpus is the gated source of the tour** — the "Rian by example" tour was *two* corpora: 19 comment-rich teaching files (`examples/rian/NN_*.rian`) that nothing verified (and that drifted — "two targets" after four shipped, `Int64` taught after `Int53` replaced it), and `Rian.Tour`'s six gated `@cells`. Decision: the teaching files carry machine-readable `#@reach`/`#@reach-pin`/`#@illustrative` headers gated against the real `Rian.Reach`, their `#=>` worked examples run as **doctests** on the BEAM (ADR-0060), and the corpus feeds `tour.json`'s `"examples"` section — so a confidently-wrong tutorial fails the build. **Refines** ADR-0058 (reach-gated honesty), ADR-0060 (executable spec-by-example), ADR-0057. **Amended 2026-06-22:** the gate also asserts **emittability** (not just reachability); the six cells became `#@pane`-tagged files (one home for source), emitter-output assertions moved to the emitter suites. Gated by `mix rian.tour --check` + `Rian.TourReachTest`/`Rian.TourDoctestTest` | **Accepted; Implemented** |
